title: Specialization datum and specialization of a correspondence
statement:
Use the finite coefficient and scheme conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$, $k$ algebraically closed and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Set $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $R=k[t]_{(t)}$, $D=\operatorname{Spec}R$, with closed point $0$, generic point $\eta$ and a chosen geometric generic point $\bar\eta$. A lift of a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $T$ is a separated finite-type $D$-scheme $\widetilde T$ with $\rho_T:\widetilde T\to T\times_kD$ whose generic fibre is an isomorphism. Write $T_0=\widetilde T\times_D0$. Choose the geometric specialization compatibly with the strict henselization $D^{\rm sh}$ at its geometric closed point [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], so that the maps
$$j_T:\widetilde T_{\bar\eta}\longrightarrow\widetilde T_{D^{\rm sh}},\qquad i_T:T_0\longrightarrow\widetilde T_{D^{\rm sh}}$$
are defined over $D$. On the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], use bounded-below constant-$A$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], exact inverse image [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], and derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For $N\in D^+((\widetilde T_\eta)_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $M\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ define
$$R\Psi_{\widetilde T}N=i_T^*Rj_{T*}N_{\bar\eta},\qquad \operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T}M=R\Psi_{\widetilde T}(\rho_{T,\eta}^*M_\eta).$$
Here the subscript $\bar\eta$ means geometric generic pullback. These are bounded-below constructions; bounded constructible finite-Tor output is not part of the definition of $\operatorname{sp}$.

For any separated finite-type map $h:V\to W$ between quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes occurring below, including maps over $D^{\rm sh}$ and $\bar\eta$, choose a compactification $V\xrightarrow{e}\overline V\xrightarrow{p}W$ (quasi-compact open $e$, proper $p$), available by [thm-nagata-compactification]. On bounded-below etale $A$-complexes use
$$Rh_!^{\mathrm{et}}=Rp_*e_!$$
of [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. This notation is independent of the compactification through the canonical comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-compactification-independence]. Compact-support base change for arbitrary quasi-compact quasi-separated base change is the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-compact-support-base-change-qcqs]. All schemes obtained here from finite-type schemes by passage to $D^{\rm sh}$ or a geometric generic fibre are quasi-compact and quasi-separated; all maps to which this notation is applied are separated and finite type.

The pro-etale realization is the comparison pullback $\nu_{T_0}^*$ of the etale construction on an etale representative. Bounded constructible pro-etale inputs admit such representatives by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]; full faithfulness on $D^+$ [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] identifies their morphisms and makes the construction independent of the representative up to the canonical isomorphism. The finite-Tor categories on the two sites are identified by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude]. When passing between etale formulas and project pro-etale operations on finite-type $k$-schemes, use
$$\nu_V^*h_{\mathrm{et}}^*\cong h_{\mathrm{proet}}^*\nu_W^*,\qquad Rh_!^{\mathrm{proet}}\nu_V^*\cong\nu_W^*Rh_!^{\mathrm{et}},$$
from [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] (termwise on constant-module complexes) and [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] respectively. The second comparison applies to every bounded-below etale input, including nearby-cycle outputs; it does not require these to be constructible. Operations over $D^{\rm sh}$ and $\bar\eta$ in the construction remain etale operations. For ordinary direct images over $k$, use the comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image].

A morphism $\widetilde f:\widetilde T\to\widetilde U$ lifts $f:T\to U$ when $\rho_U\widetilde f=(f\times\operatorname{id}_D)\rho_T$; write $f_0=\widetilde f_0$. For such a lifted morphism define on bounded-below etale complexes
$$\mathrm{BC}^*:f_0^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde U}\longrightarrow\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T}f^*,\qquad \mathrm{BC}_*:\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde U}Rf_*\longrightarrow Rf_{0*}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T},$$
$$\mathrm{BC}_!:Rf_{0!}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T}\longrightarrow\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde U}Rf_!.$$
The first is $i_T^*$ applied to the ordinary exchange $\widetilde f_{D^{\rm sh}}^*Rj_{U*}\to Rj_{T*}\widetilde f_{\bar\eta}^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], in constant-module coefficients as in [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients], followed by pullback composition. The third is the composite
$$Rf_{0!}i_T^*Rj_{T*}\xrightarrow{\sim}i_U^*R\widetilde f_{D^{\rm sh}!}Rj_{T*}\longrightarrow i_U^*Rj_{U*}R\widetilde f_{\bar\eta!},$$
where the first arrow is the inverse compact-support base-change isomorphism along $i_U$. The second is $i_U^*$ of the morphism adjoint under $j_U^*\dashv Rj_{U*}$ to
$$j_U^*R\widetilde f_{D^{\rm sh}!}Rj_{T*}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\widetilde f_{\bar\eta!}j_T^*Rj_{T*}\xrightarrow{R\widetilde f_{\bar\eta!}(\varepsilon_{j_T})}R\widetilde f_{\bar\eta!}.$$
The isomorphism in this formula is compact-support base change along $j_U$. In the right-hand side of $\mathrm{BC}_!$, identify $R\widetilde f_{\bar\eta!}$ on the generic input with $(Rf_!(-))_{\bar\eta}$ using the lift isomorphisms and compact-support base change along $U_{\bar\eta}\to U$. All three base-change isomorphisms are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-compact-support-base-change-qcqs], with the compactification comparisons above. Define $\mathrm{BC}_*$ as the mate of $\mathrm{BC}^*$ under ordinary derived adjunctions, with mate as in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]; the derived adjunction is [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction], in constant modules as in [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients].

Use $Rf^!$ and $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ on $D^b_{ctf}$ as specified by [def-trf-admissibility]. At an input $L\in D^b_{ctf}(U,A)$ for which both $\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde U}L$ and $\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T}Rf^!L$ lie in the corresponding $D^b_{ctf}$ categories, define
$$\mathrm{BC}^!_L:\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T}Rf^!L\longrightarrow Rf_0^!\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde U}L$$
as the exceptional adjoint of
$$Rf_{0!}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T}Rf^!L\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BC}_!}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde U}Rf_!Rf^!L\xrightarrow{\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde U}(\varepsilon_f)}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde U}L.$$
On subcategories where the specialization functors land in $D^b_{ctf}$ this is the mate of $\mathrm{BC}_!$. No such finiteness hypothesis is used to define $\mathrm{BC}^*$, $\mathrm{BC}_*$ or $\mathrm{BC}_!$.

Put $\omega_T=Ra_T^!A_s$ as in [def-trf-dualizing-complex], and use the Borel--Moore sections $\alpha:A_T\to\omega_T$ of [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward]. Let $\operatorname{can}_T:A_{T_0}\to\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T}A_T$ be $i_T^*$ applied to the unit $A_{\widetilde T_{D^{\rm sh}}}\to Rj_{T*}j_T^*A_{\widetilde T_{D^{\rm sh}}}$. For the constant lift $D$ of $s$ the map $\operatorname{can}_s:A_s\to\operatorname{sp}_DA_s$ is invertible: $D^{\rm sh}$ is strictly henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-local-structure], the germ map at its closed point identifies sections with the stalk by [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk], and [lem-kun-0ezp] applied to $j_s:\bar\eta\to D^{\rm sh}$ gives $R^qj_{s*}A=0$ for $q>0$. Consequently
$$i_s^*Rj_{s*}A=\Gamma(D^{\rm sh},j_{s*}A)=\Gamma(\bar\eta,A)=A,$$
concentrated in degree zero: the last equality follows because $\bar\eta$ is a separably closed point and a constant sheaf there has sections $A$. Under these identifications the unit sends each $a\in A$ to $a$, so $\operatorname{can}_s$ is the identity on $A$.

Define the Borel--Moore specialization of $\alpha$ to be the adjoint under $Ra_{T_0!}\dashv Ra_{T_0}^!$ of the following morphism from $Ra_{T_0!}A_{T_0}$ to $A_s$:
$$\begin{aligned}
Ra_{T_0!}A_{T_0}&\xrightarrow{Ra_{T_0!}(\operatorname{can}_T)}Ra_{T_0!}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T}A_T\\
&\xrightarrow{Ra_{T_0!}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T}(\alpha)}Ra_{T_0!}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T}\omega_T\\
&\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BC}_!}\operatorname{sp}_DRa_{T!}\omega_T\xrightarrow{\operatorname{sp}_D(\varepsilon_{a_T})}\operatorname{sp}_DA_s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{can}_s^{-1}}A_s.
\end{aligned}$$
The $\mathrm{BC}_!$ here belongs to the lifted structure morphism $\widetilde T\to D$, and $\varepsilon_{a_T}:Ra_{T!}\omega_T\to A_s$ is its original-fibre exceptional counit. This defines
$$\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T}:\operatorname{Hom}(A_T,\omega_T)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(A_{T_0},\omega_{T_0})$$
for every lift: intermediate nearby cycles are used only with bounded-below compact support, while the final exceptional adjunction has the $D^b_{ctf}$ input $A_{T_0}$ and target $A_s$.

If $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_kX$ of [def-trf-correspondence] has a lift $\widetilde c:\widetilde C\to\widetilde X\times_D\widetilde X$, write $b=(b_1,b_2)=\widetilde c_0$. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, $u:c_2^*K\to c_1^!K$, and $\widehat u:Rc_{1!}c_2^*K\to K$ its exceptional adjoint. When $\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X}K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_0,A)$, define the specialized coefficient morphism to be the exceptional adjoint of
$$Rb_{1!}b_2^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X}K\xrightarrow{Rb_{1!}\mathrm{BC}^*}Rb_{1!}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde C}c_2^*K\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BC}_!}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X}Rc_{1!}c_2^*K\xrightarrow{\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X}(\widehat u)}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X}K.$$
Indeed $b_2^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X}K$ is in $D^b_{ctf}$ by [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], so the exceptional adjunction for $b_1$ applies to the endpoints. The middle terms remain in the bounded-below etale-origin categories and need no constructibility assertion. This defines
$$\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde c}u:b_2^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X}K\longrightarrow b_1^!\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X}K$$
under the stated finite-Tor constructibility condition.

from.place: Proof paragraph (1) and (2): Varshavsky specialization to the normal cone, §§1.3–1.4, supplying the specialization functor and its correspondence base-change maps.

split_report.summary: Repaired the returned E1/E5 finiteness/type error: nearby cycles and the three ordinary/compact-support exchanges are defined on bounded-below etale complexes; BC^! is conditional on its relevant specialization values lying in D^b_ctf, and specialization of a correspondence is conditional on sp_X K lying there. Borel--Moore specialization for every lift is instead the adjoint of the compact-support/unit/BC_!/counit/point-normalization composite, so no exceptional adjoint is applied to an arbitrary nearby-cycle value. Added existing nodes defining compact-support etale functors on qcqs schemes and proving compactification independence and arbitrary qcqs base change, explicitly for i_U, j_U and geometric generic pullback. Added the actual pullback/direct-image/compact-support etale--proetale comparison statements, full faithfulness and Tor comparison. Normalization at the point is justified by the existing strict-henselian sections--stalk theorem and the separably closed field direct-image vanishing, with the degree-zero unit calculated. All earlier Mathlib searches are retained; the changed finiteness/compact-support formulation was searched again and no match found. No new nodes, no Lean work, no prohibited source, and no unit-route change.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the specialization datum used in the proof of lem-trf-local-term-locality: Varshavsky §§1.3.1–1.3.4 define lifts, nearby-cycle specialization, Borel–Moore specialization, base-change maps, and specialization of correspondence morphisms.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q129-25e6e78cd (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS: the repair is correct and matches Varshavsky. I read the item in full (no new nodes), all 28 cited statements, all 7 citers, the ancestor lem-trf-local-term-locality, unit sk-i-curve-zero, and Varshavsky arXiv math/0505564 §§1.3.1–1.3.4 and Prop 1.3.5 (pp. 10–13). (1) Nearby cycles i^*Rj_* from the geometric generic fibre to T̃_{D^sh}, and sp = RΨ(ρ_η^*M_η), match 1.3.1(e) and 1.3.2(a); the larger D^+ domain weakens nothing. (2) BC^* has the right orientation as the exchange for the cartesian square (j_U, j_T). (3) BC_! is the source's composite with its mate written out. Its three compact-support base changes (along i_U, j_U and U_η̄→U) meet the hypotheses of lem-weil-pbc-etale-compact-support-base-change-qcqs: separated finite-type maps, qcqs bases, finite A. (4) BC^! is defined only where both endpoints are in D^b_ctf, the domain of the restricted adjunction in def-trf-admissibility. (5) The Borel–Moore specialisation is the transpose of Varshavsky 1.3.3(b) BC^!∘BC_*; they agree because the exchange is compatible with units (BC^*∘can_D = can_T) and BC^! is the mate of BC_!. Its only exceptional adjunction has the ctf endpoints A_{T0} and A_s. (6) can_s is the identity on A, by strict henselianity, the sections–stalk lemma and lem-kun-0ezp (R^q j_*=0); there is no cycle through the zero-section lemma. (7) The correspondence coefficient is 1.3.4 with the legs swapped; b_2^*spK is ctf by lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude; no properness or invertibility of u is added. (8) The étale/pro-étale comparisons are applied only over finite-type k-schemes, and full faithfulness on D^+ needs no constructibility. All 7 citers stay well-typed: those using sp_c u assume or prove sp K ctf. The report counted only 3 citers; this is a reporting slip only. No dependency cycle, no duplicate node or blueprint node, three kinds of Mathlib search recorded, no SGA. Edge cases checked: M=0, empty special fibre, constant point lift, n=1, non-proper lifts. Minor: the item has no lean_audit field, inherited from the base node. No fixes made.
